1.title: Quick-Reference Recap and Decision Chooser
1.text: Welcome to Module seventeen: Quick-Reference Recap and Decision Chooser. This module covers quick-reference recap and decision chooser. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. One-page decision tables for each domain. The names, numbers and limits worth memorizing. The distractor patterns that make wrong answers attractive.

1.title: Case Check-In: Cedarbrook Outfitters
1.text: Our running case is Cedarbrook Outfitters. Cedarbrook Outfitters. The team meets the topic of this module. Your job: decide, step by step, which choice fits best.

1.title: Decision Chooser
1.text: Decision Chooser. The figure shows this: The decision chooser: for each recurring decision, ask the deciding question and pick the matching answer.

1.title: D1 Prompting and D2 Output Evaluation (35%)
1.text: D one Prompting and D two Output Evaluation (thirty-five percent). Generic or weak answer. Best move: Add goal, audience, context, format, constraints, example. Deciding question: Did the prompt say what a good result is? Big, multi-part request. Best move: Decompose: plan, parts, combine, review. Deciding question: Can each step be checked? Output not right. Best move: Specific feedback, change one thing, keep what works. Deciding question: Which exact thing should change? Thread drifted or very long. Best move: Summarize and restart. Deciding question: Are early decisions being lost? Brainstorm. Best move: Many varied options, judge later. Deciding question: Is quantity the goal? Factual or analytic task. Best move: Sources, assumptions, shown figures, verify. Deciding question: Can I check it?

1.title: D1 Prompting and D2 Output Evaluation (35%), continued
1.text: D one Prompting and D two Output Evaluation (thirty-five percent), continued. Confident claim, citation, number. Best move: Verify in the primary source; recalculate. Deciding question: Where is the evidence? Same message, different readers. Best move: Adapt delivery, keep facts. Deciding question: Did any fact change? High stakes, people, regulated, external. Best move: Qualified human review (and disclosure). Deciding question: Who is accountable? Reusable, editable deliverable. Best move: Artifact or file; data for another tool: structured table. Deciding question: Will it be edited, reused or shared?

1.title: D3 Product and Model Selection (12%)
1.text: D three Product and Model Selection (twelve percent). Single current fact. Web search. Hard reasoning, no web needed. Extended thinking. Comprehensive cited report. Research. Questions about your files. Upload (P D F up to one thousand pages; one hundred pages for visuals). Recurring background. Project. High-volume simple tasks. Haiku-type: fast, low cost. Everyday work. Sonnet-type: balanced. Complex, nuanced, long work. Opus-type (or the top tier): capable, slower. Routine task. Lower effort; hard task: higher effort or thinking. Context crowded. Restart or summarize; persist stable facts in Projects, memory, documents.

1.title: D4 Workflow and D5 Configuration (28%)
1.text: D four Workflow and D five Configuration (twenty-eight percent). Vague business complaint. Clarify into requirements, list assumptions, validate with people. Choosing use cases. High value, low risk first; human review where errors matter. Plan from Claude. Check against real capacity; ask for options. Improving a process. Map, find bottlenecks, redesign, pilot, measure. Add Claude to a workflow. Augment a step with draft-and-review first; redesign after a pilot. A P I (application programming interface), agents, systems integration, security architecture. Escalate to Developer or Architect with a brief. Tell stakeholders. Evidence-based value and plain limits, review plan. Standing instructions and knowledge. Project; instructions with role, audience, format, rules, source of truth, uncertainty, escalation.

1.title: D4 Workflow and D5 Configuration (28%), continued
1.text: D four Workflow and D five Configuration (twenty-eight percent), continued. Repeatable method. Skill (trusted sources). Live data in Drive or Gmail. Connector, narrow scope, approvals. Policy or product changes. Update knowledge and instructions, test, tell the team, version.

1.title: D6 Governance (15%) and D7 Troubleshooting (10%)
1.text: D six Governance (fifteen percent) and D seven Troubleshooting (ten percent). Personal or regulated data. Remove or anonymize, minimize, approved tool and account, follow policy. Hiring, credit, benefits, medical, legal. Qualified human decides; bias review; disclose A I use. Fake reviews, deception, unauthorized access. Decline. Policy silent. Ask the policy owner, Legal or Privacy. Data exposed. Contain, report, record. Output weak. Diagnose: observe, pattern, cause, change one thing, test. Claude claims an action. Check the destination; is there an integration? Slow or limit reached. Lower effort or lighter model, fewer tools, new short chat, wait for reset.

1.title: D6 Governance (15%) and D7 Troubleshooting (10%), continued
1.text: D six Governance (fifteen percent) and D seven Troubleshooting (ten percent), continued. Optimize a workflow. Baseline, change one thing, pilot, compare; standardize with templates, Projects, Skills. Exam tip: When two options both work, prefer the one that verifies, protects data, fits the task and keeps a person accountable.

1.title: Names and Values to Know
1.text: Names and Values to Know. Exam. C C A O F; sixty items; one hundred twenty min; seven hundred twenty of one thousand; U S D ninety-nine; valid twelve months. Domain weights. D two twenty-one, D four sixteen, D six fifteen, D one fourteen, D three twelve, D five twelve, D seven ten. Models. Haiku fast and low cost, Sonnet balanced, Opus most capable of the three. Research. five or more lookups, about one to three minutes, cited report, paid plans. Free-plan Projects. five. R A G for Projects. Paid plans; up to about ten times capacity. Chat file limits. twenty files, five hundred megabytes each, P D F up to one thousand pages (visuals analyzed up to one hundred pages). Project files. About thirty megabytes each.

1.title: Names and Values to Know, continued
1.text: Names and Values to Know, continued. Created files. About thirty megabytes. Usage limits. Five-hour session limit and weekly limits on paid plans. Incognito. Not in history, memory or training; outside Projects; kept thirty days. Memory. On by default (individual plans); per-Project memory; sensitive topics off by default. Artifacts. Private by default; Docs, Slides, Design, Dashboards (beta); storage twenty megabytes text only. Skills. Folder with a description (two hundred characters max) and instructions; need code execution. Connectors. Your permissions; approval for send, share, trash; Auto, Always available, On demand. Exam tip: Numbers matter most where they decide a feature choice: Research is for five or more lookups, a Project holds standing background, and incognito is not an exemption from policy.

1.title: Names and Values to Know, continued
1.text: Names and Values to Know, continued. Plan names, limits, model names and menu labels change; the principles behind them are what the questions test.

1.title: Distractor Patterns
1.text: Distractor Patterns. "Claude sounded confident, so send it". Why it is tempting: Fluent text feels reliable. Why it fails: Confidence is not evidence; verify. "Ask Claude if it is sure". Why it is tempting: Quick. Why it fails: Not independent validation. "Always use the biggest model or highest effort". Why it is tempting: More power seems safer. Why it fails: Slower, costs usage, unnecessary. "Always use the smallest". Why it is tempting: Cheap and fast. Why it fails: Fails on hard reasoning. "Research for everything". Why it is tempting: Sounds thorough. Why it fails: Overkill for a simple fact. "Keep going in the same long chat". Why it is tempting: No setup. Why it fails: Context drifts; restart or summarize. "Paste the background each time". Why it is tempting: Works today. Why it fails: Wasteful; use a Project.

1.title: Distractor Patterns, continued
1.text: Distractor Patterns, continued. "Tell Claude not to retain the data". Why it is tempting: Feels protective. Why it fails: Not a policy control; remove or anonymize. "It's internal, so it's fine". Why it is tempting: Familiar data. Why it fails: Internal can still be regulated or confidential. "Incognito means exempt from policy". Why it is tempting: Sounds private. Why it fails: Policy and retention still apply. "Let Claude decide people matters". Why it is tempting: Fast. Why it fails: Needs qualified human and disclosure. "Hide A I use". Why it is tempting: Avoids questions. Why it fails: Transparency is expected. "Build the integration yourself". Why it is tempting: Eager. Why it fails: Escalate A P I and architecture work. "Rewrite everything". Why it is tempting: Feels thorough. Why it fails: Change one thing and retest. "Skip review to save time". Why it is tempting: Efficiency. Why it fails: Efficiency without quality is not optimization. Exam tip: A distractor often sounds efficient (skip the check, paste everything, use the biggest model); the correct answer is usually the one that keeps quality, data safety and accountability.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Prompt: Goal, context, audience, format, constraints, example. Work: Decompose, iterate with specific feedback, adapt to task type. Evaluate: Accurate, complete, consistent, unbiased, verified outside Claude. Review: Scale with stakes; qualified human for high-risk uses. Features: Web search (fact), thinking (reasoning), Research (report), files, Projects, artifacts, Skills, connectors. Models: Haiku fast or cheap, Sonnet balanced, Opus capable; match to task. Context: Restart, summarize, persist. Config: Project (background), Skill (procedure), connector (live data); maintain and test. Governance: Policy first, classify data, minimize, human accountable, transparency. Fix: Diagnose, change one thing, test. Optimize: Lighter and reusable and measured, with review kept. In the next module, we continue the course.
